# Abstract {#front:abstract}

Machine learning models are trained once but used for months or years. In that time the data they see in production slowly stops looking like the data they were trained on. When this happens accuracy falls, often without anyone noticing, because the true labels that would reveal the loss arrive weeks or months later. Existing monitoring tools can raise an alarm when the data change, but they rarely say what kind of change took place. This matters because each kind calls for a different response: a change in the inputs alone may need only reweighting, a change in the class balance needs recalibration, a change in the relationship between inputs and labels needs fresh labels and corrupted labels point to a fault in the labeling process.

ResilientAI is an end-to-end monitoring system that answers these questions for every new batch of production data. It tests whether the data have changed, estimates the lost accuracy from the model's own confidence, finds the features that moved and names the drift type with a sequence of statistical tests that share one stated error rate. A first stage needs no labels and separates input shift from class balance shift. A second stage, new in this project, uses a few hundred late labels to separate concept drift from label noise. The system also explains the change, scores how far each single prediction can be trusted and advises whether a cheap retrain would help. An interactive dashboard presents every result.

On a benchmark of drift injected into two census tasks, the system named the drift type in \res{bench-a-ours-min} to \res{bench-a-ours-max}% of windows and stayed at \res{bench-b-ours-min} to \res{bench-b-ours-max}% on drift mechanisms it was not designed for, where a learned rule fell to \res{bench-b-meta-min} to \res{bench-b-meta-max}%. On four real datasets with documented changes it raised no false alarm on any control window and traced the known events.

**Keywords:** concept drift, dataset shift, model monitoring, drift diagnosis, hypothesis testing, machine learning operations
